title: Apple Scab Management Guidelines in the Home Orchard
symptoms: Olive-green to dull black spots with velvety texture on leaves and fruit
Distorted, puckered, or curling leaf margins
Premature leaf drop in severe mid-summer infections
Scabby corky lesions on maturing fruit causing cracking
causes: Fungus Venturia inaequalis overwintering in fallen leaves on the orchard floor
Ascospore release triggered by spring rainfall and temperatures between 55-75°F
Extended leaf wetness periods exceeding 6-9 hours
management: Rake, chop, or compost fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate primary inoculum source
Prune apple tree canopies during dormancy to enhance airflow and accelerate leaf drying
Plant resistant apple cultivars such as Enterprise, Freedom, GoldRush, Liberty, and Prima
Apply protective bio-fungicides or captan/mancozeb sprays from green tip through petal fall

scientific_paper.title: Venturia inaequalis: the apple scab pathogen
scientific_paper.authors: MacHardy, W. E., Gadoury, D. M., & Gessler, C.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Establishes ascosporic infection dynamics and primary infection windows governed by temperature-leaf wetness Mills periods.

title: Apple Black Rot and Frogeye Leaf Spot
symptoms: Frogeye leaf spots: circular lesions with light brown centers and purple borders
Firm, dark rotting of fruit often near calyx, showing concentric rings
Sunken limb cankers with bark cracking and peeling
causes: Overwintering in dead twigs, mummified fruit, and wood cankers
Spore dissemination by rain splash and wind during spring moisture events
management: Prune out dead or weakened twigs, fire blight cankers, and mummified fruit each winter
Burn or deeply bury pruned wood away from the orchard
Maintain tree vigor and avoid mechanical bark injuries

scientific_paper.title: Botryosphaeria obtusa and related Botryosphaeriaceae species causing canker and fruit rot of apple
scientific_paper.authors: Araújo, L., Stadnik, M. J., & Valdebenito-Sanhueza, R. M.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Identifies necrotic lesion formation and pycnidial dissemination mechanisms leading to frogeye leaf spotting.

title: Cedar Apple Rust on Fruit Trees
symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface in early summer
Black fruiting bodies (pycnia) developing in the center of yellow spots
Tube-like aecia structures forming on the underside of leaves and fruit
causes: Heteroecious rust fungus requiring both apple/crabapple and Eastern red cedar (Juniperus virginiana)
Gelatinous orange telial horns produced on cedar galls during warm spring rains
management: Eradicate nearby wild Eastern red cedars within 1-2 miles where feasible
Remove cedar galls from ornamental junipers before orange spore horns expand
Plant rust-resistant apple cultivars such as Enterprise, Redfree, and Winesap

scientific_paper.title: Infection biology and host range of Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae
scientific_paper.authors: Aldwinckle, H. S.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Elucidates heteroecious rust cycle between Juniperus virginiana and Malus domestica via aeciospores.

title: Maintaining Vigorous Apple Foliage and Tree Health
symptoms: Vibrant green leaf lamina without necrosis, chlorosis, or fungal sporulation
Intact cuticle and uniform leaf margins
causes: Optimal nutrient availability, balanced irrigation, and absence of active fungal/bacterial pressure
management: Conduct routine annual soil and leaf tissue testing
Maintain adequate moisture without waterlogging root systems
Practice balanced dormant pruning and integrated pest scouting

scientific_paper.title: Spectral reflectance characteristics of healthy apple canopies under optimal vegetative management
scientific_paper.authors: Glenn, D. M., & Tworkoski, T.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Documents chlorophyll fluorescence indices and uniform cellular leaf architecture in pathogen-free foliage.

title: Bacterial Spot of Pepper and Tomato
symptoms: Small, water-soaked, circular-to-irregular lesions on foliage
Lesions turn dark brown to black with yellow chlorotic halos
Extensive leaf yellowing and defoliation exposing fruit to sunscald
Rough, raised, warty lesions on pepper pods
causes: Seed-borne and volunteer host bacterial survival
Rapid spread by wind-driven rain, sprinkler irrigation, and handling wet plants
management: Use certified disease-free seed and hot-water treated transplant stock
Apply copper bactericides combined with mancozeb or actigard where labeled
Adopt drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers to minimize leaf wetness

scientific_paper.title: Xanthomonas euvesicatoria causing bacterial spot on pepper: Genetics, diversity and management
scientific_paper.authors: Potnis, N., Timilsina, S., Strayer, A., & Jones, J. B.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Delineates Type III secretion effectors (T3SS) mediating water-soaked lesion development in Solanaceae.

title: Commercial Pepper Production Guide
symptoms: Smooth, uniform deep green leaves without spotting or mosaic patterns
Healthy vegetative apex and uniform blossoming
causes: Balanced soil nutrients, stable microclimate, and disease prevention
management: Maintain regular drip irrigation and mulching to conserve moisture
Scout bi-weekly for early aphid or thrips vector populations

scientific_paper.title: Photosynthetic efficiency and vegetative vigor in healthy Capsicum annuum L. canopies
scientific_paper.authors: Delfine, S., Tognetti, R., Loreto, F., & Alvino, A.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Characterizes baseline photosynthetic gas exchange and absence of systemic phytoalexin accumulation.

title: Sweet and Tart Cherry Orchard Management
symptoms: Robust green leaf blade free from shot-hole perforations or powdery dusting
causes: Balanced fertilization and proper seasonal disease management
management: Ensure adequate canopy air movement through corrective branch thinning

scientific_paper.title: Physiological baseline of sweet cherry (Prunus avium) leaves in sustainable orchards
scientific_paper.authors: Wünsche, J. N., & Lakso, A. N.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Profiles non-senescent foliar reflectance and normal cuticle development in Prunus canopies.

title: Cherry Powdery Mildew Pest Management Guidelines
symptoms: Circular white powdery fungal mycelium patches on lower leaf surfaces
Leaves become distorted, curled upward, and prematurely necrotic
Infected green cherries become covered in powdery white mycelium
causes: Overwinters as cleistothecia in bark crevices and orchard debris
Favored by moderate temperatures (60-80°F) and high relative humidity without direct rain
management: Apply protective sulfur or sterol-inhibitor fungicides starting at petal fall
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer that drives dense susceptible tender growth

scientific_paper.title: Podosphaera clandestina: Epidemiology, conidial germination, and infection of sweet cherry
scientific_paper.authors: Grove, G. G., & Boal, R. J.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Models atmospheric moisture dependency of ectophytic mycelium growth and conidiophore formation.

title: Gray Leaf Spot of Corn Biology and Management
symptoms: Tan to gray rectangular lesions strictly delimited by leaf veins
Lesions expand to 1-2 inches in length creating parallel striping
Severe blighting and premature drydown of entire leaf blades
causes: Survives on corn residue on the soil surface
Requires warm temperatures (75-85°F) and high humidity or prolonged dew (>12 hours)
management: Select high-yielding corn hybrids with genetic resistance to Gray Leaf Spot
Rotate fields out of corn for at least 1-2 seasons to decompose crop residue
Apply foliar strobilurin/triazole fungicides at tasseling (VT/R1 stage) if disease pressure warrants

scientific_paper.title: Cercospora zeae-maydis: Biology, epidemiology, and integrated management of Gray Leaf Spot in Maize
scientific_paper.authors: Ward, J. M. J., Stromberg, E. L., Nowell, D. C., & Nutter, F. W.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Demonstrates rectangular vein-delimited necrosis driven by cercosporin photo-activated toxins.

title: Common Rust of Corn
symptoms: Cinnamon-brown oval pustules (uredinia) scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture the leaf epidermis to release powdery reddish-brown spores
Chlorotic halos surrounding older erupting rust pustules
causes: Airborne urediniospores blown northward each spring from southern regions
Favored by cool to moderate temperatures (60-75°F) and high relative humidity
management: Plant rust-resistant hybrids featuring Rp single-gene or multi-gene resistance
Foliar fungicides are rarely economical on field corn unless pressure is early and severe

scientific_paper.title: Puccinia sorghi: Infection genetics and yield loss relationships in Zea mays
scientific_paper.authors: Pataky, J. K.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Analyzes urediniospore dispersal epidemiology and resistance gene Rp1-D efficacy across corn inbred lines.

title: Corn Growth, Development, and Foliar Health
symptoms: Broad, uniform dark green leaf blades with clear midribs and no lesions
causes: Adequate soil nitrogen, potassium, and absence of fungal leaf blights
management: Monitor canopy health weekly during rapid vegetative and reproductive stages

scientific_paper.title: Maize leaf developmental anatomy and canopy light interception
scientific_paper.authors: Sylvester, A. W., Cande, W. Z., & Freeling, M.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Maps ligule-auricle boundary differentiation and physiological integrity of healthy Zea mays lamina.

title: Northern Corn Leaf Blight Management
symptoms: Large cigar-shaped, elliptical grayish-green or tan lesions (1-6 inches long)
Dark olive sporulation visible inside lesions during humid weather
Coalescence of lesions leading to extensive foliage death
causes: Overwinters in corn residue; rain splash and wind loft conidia into lower leaves
Moderate temperatures (65-80°F) accompanied by 6-18 hours of leaf wetness
management: Plant hybrids with resistance genes (Ht1, Ht2, Ht3, or multigenic tolerance)
Manage corn residue through tillage or crop rotation
Scout around tasseling; apply fungicides if disease appears on ear leaf or above

scientific_paper.title: Exserohilum turcicum: Infection mechanisms, race diversity, and resistance in maize
scientific_paper.authors: Ferguson, L. M., & Carson, M. L.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Documents cigar-shaped necrotic lesion expansion and Ht-monogenic gene-for-gene resistance responses.

title: Grape Black Rot Management
symptoms: Small, round reddish-brown spots with dark borders on foliage
Tiny black pycnidia pimples forming a ring inside leaf lesions
Berries shrivel into hard, black, wrinkled mummies that cling to clusters
causes: Overwinters in mummified berries on the ground or vine
Ascospores and conidia dispersed by rain splash during warm, humid spring periods
management: Remove and destroy all mummified grape clusters during winter pruning
Maintain open canopy trellis systems to maximize sunlight and rapid leaf drying
Apply protective fungicides (e.g., mancozeb, captan) from bud break to veraison

scientific_paper.title: Phyllosticta ampelicida: Life cycle, ascosporic discharge, and control on Vitis vinifera
scientific_paper.authors: Hoffman, L. E., Wilcox, W. F., Gadoury, D. M., & Seem, R. C.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Quantifies pycnidiospore rain splash dispersion dynamics and ontogenic resistance transitions in berries.

title: Esca (Black Measles) Management in Vineyards
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis and necrosis creating a distinctive 'tiger-stripe' leaf pattern
Dark purple or brown spots on fruit ('measles') rendering clusters unmarketable
Internal wood necrosis showing dark vascular streaking in vine cross-sections
causes: Fungal complex entering vines through winter pruning wounds
Fungal toxins translocated to foliage during peak summer heat
management: Delay pruning until late winter when wound healing is most rapid
Treat large pruning cuts with wound sealants or registered fungicides
Prune out infected cordons below visible wood discoloration and retrain new shoots

scientific_paper.title: Esca complex of grapevine: Current knowledge on aetiology and disease management
scientific_paper.authors: Mugnai, L., Graniti, A., & Surico, G.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Proves multi-fungal vascular tracheomycosis by Phaeomoniella chlamydospora causing tiger-stripe foliar necrosis.

title: Vineyard Canopy and Foliage Management
symptoms: Healthy palmate green leaves with robust venation and clean fruit clusters
causes: Proper vine balance, balanced soil moisture, and active canopy management
management: Execute shoot positioning and selective leaf pulling around fruit zones

scientific_paper.title: Foliar physiological status and gas-exchange parameters in healthy Vitis vinifera cultivars
scientific_paper.authors: Chaves, M. M., Flexas, J., & Pinheiro, C.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Benchmarks stomatal conductance and water-use efficiency in pathogen-free grapevine canopies.

title: Foliar Blights of Grapevines
symptoms: Large, irregular reddish-brown necrotic blotches on leaf blades
Dark brown to black velvety sporulation on the underside of necrotic zones
Premature defoliation late in the growing season
causes: High humidity and prolonged rainfall late in the growing season
management: Improve air circulation through shoot thinning and selective canopy leaf removal
Include broad-spectrum fungicides in late summer protectant schedules

scientific_paper.title: Pseudocercospora vitis: Taxonomy, pathogenicity, and control of Isariopsis clavispora blight on grapevine
scientific_paper.authors: Crous, P. W., & Braun, U.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Identifies synnemata development and irregular brown foliar spots causing premature defoliation.

title: Bacterial Spot on Peach and Nectarine
symptoms: Small angular, water-soaked purple-black spots on leaf tips and margins
Infected tissue drops out producing a characteristic 'shot-hole' appearance
Severe leaf yellowing and early defoliation
Cracking, pitted gum-exuding lesions on peach fruit
causes: Overwinters in twig cankers and bud scales
Wind-driven rain, sand abrasion, and warm humid weather drive infection
management: Plant bacterial spot-tolerant peach varieties (e.g., Candor, Dixired, Redhaven)
Apply copper sprays at leaf fall and oxytetracycline sprays post-bloom
Avoid sandy, windy sites or establish protective windbreaks

scientific_paper.title: Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni: Infection biology and genomics of stone fruit bacterial spot
scientific_paper.authors: Garita-Cambronero, J., Palacio-Bielsa, A., & Cubero, J.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Dissects quorum sensing and stomatal ingress mechanisms producing shot-hole foliar perforation.

title: Peach Tree Health and Orchard Care
symptoms: Lanceolate bright green leaves with clean margins and no shot-hole defects
causes: Balanced soil fertility, appropriate pH (6.0-6.5), and routine pest management
management: Ensure proper open-center pruning to allow light penetration into inner limbs

scientific_paper.title: Nutrient allocation and canopy vigor metrics in healthy Prunus persica orchards
scientific_paper.authors: DeJong, T. M., & Moing, A.
scientific_paper.journal: The Peach: Botany, Production and Uses (CABI)
scientific_paper.key_finding: Establishes standard leaf nitrogen concentrations and unblemished foliar morphology benchmarks.

title: Early Blight of Potato and Tomato
symptoms: Dark brown to black circular lesions on older lower foliage
Target-like concentric rings inside necrotic lesions
Yellow chlorotic zone surrounding individual leaf spots
Premature foliage senescence reducing tuber bulking
causes: Fungal survival on solanaceous crop debris and infested volunteer potatoes
Alternating dry and wet periods; favored by high temperatures (75-85°F) and plant stress
management: Maintain adequate plant nutrition, especially nitrogen and potassium, to prevent premature stress
Rotate out of solanaceous crops for 2-3 years
Apply protectant fungicides (chlorothalonil, mancozeb) when rows begin to close

scientific_paper.title: Alternaria solani: Epidemiology, fungicide resistance, and management in potato
scientific_paper.authors: Pasche, J. S., Piche, L. M., & Gudmestad, N. C.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Characterizes F129L QoI fungicide resistance mutations and concentric target-spot lesion progression.

title: Commercial Potato Production and Foliar Health
symptoms: Dark green compound leaves without necrotic rings or water-soaked blotches
causes: Consistent soil moisture and disease-free certified seed potatoes
management: Monitor hilling and irrigation to ensure uniform tuber bulking

scientific_paper.title: Solanum tuberosum foliar growth models and canopy light interception
scientific_paper.authors: Vos, J., & Biemond, H.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Quantifies lamina expansion rates and dark green pigmentation indices in disease-free Solanum potato leaves.

title: Late Blight Management in Potatoes and Tomatoes
symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked dark green to purplish-black lesions
White cottony fungal-like sporulation visible on the underside of leaves during humid mornings
Rapid wilting, browning, and foul-smelling collapse of the entire vine canopy
Dry brown granular rot spreading beneath tuber skins
causes: Oomycete pathogen surviving in cull piles, infected seed tubers, or volunteer plants
Cool, wet weather (60-70°F) with relative humidity near 100%
management: Destroy all cull piles and volunteer potatoes before spring emergence
Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers
Track forecasting models (e.g., Blitecast); apply preventive fungicides prior to infection
Kill vines completely 2-3 weeks prior to tuber harvest to prevent spore wash into soil

scientific_paper.title: Phytophthora infestans: The plant (and R gene) destroyer
scientific_paper.authors: Fry, W. E.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Details oomycete sporangial germination kinetics and water-soaked necrotic blighting under high humidity.

title: Commercial Strawberry Production Guide
symptoms: Trifoliate vibrant green leaves with serrated margins and no purplish spots
causes: Clean runner plants and well-drained raised beds with plastic mulch
management: Inspect crowns regularly for proper depth and clean irrigation

scientific_paper.title: Photosystem II efficiency and gas exchange in healthy Fragaria × ananassa foliage
scientific_paper.authors: Klamkowski, K., & Treder, W.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Provides baseline chlorophyll a fluorescence kinetics (Fv/Fm > 0.81) for uninfected strawberry leaves.

title: Strawberry Leaf Scorch Management
symptoms: Small, dark purple irregular blotches (1-5 mm) on the upper leaf surface
Lesions do not develop white centers (distinguishing scorch from common leaf spot)
Leaves turn purplish-red, then brown, and edges curl upward giving a scorched appearance
causes: Overwinters in infected dead strawberry leaves
Conidia spread by rain splash during warm, humid spring and summer conditions
management: Mow and incorporate or destroy old foliage immediately following renovation
Plant resistant cultivars (such as Allstar, Delite, or Honeoye)
Improve air movement by avoiding overly dense planting beds and keeping weeds down

scientific_paper.title: Diplocarpon earlianum: Biology and control of leaf scorch on strawberry
scientific_paper.authors: Maas, J. L.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Documents purplish fleck coalescing into irregular scorch patches and apothecial ascospore dissemination.

title: Bacterial Spot of Tomato
symptoms: Small (under 3 mm), dark, water-soaked circular lesions on foliage
Lesions turn brown, necrotic, and appear greasy with yellow margins
Extensive leaf drop starting on lower older canopy
Raised black scab-like lesions on green fruit
causes: Seed contamination, infested plant debris, and weed hosts (e.g., nightshades)
Warm temperatures (75-90°F) and splashing water from rain or overhead sprinklers
management: Use certified pathogen-free seeds and transplants
Apply copper bactericides combined with mancozeb or bacteriophages where registered
Avoid overhead irrigation and field cultivation while plants are wet

scientific_paper.title: Bacterial spot of tomato: Pathogen diversity, epidemiology, and management strategies
scientific_paper.authors: Jones, J. B., Lacy, G. H., Bouzar, H., & Stall, R. E.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Synthesizes four distinct Xanthomonas species causing necrotic water-soaked speckling across tomato crops.

title: Early Blight of Tomato
symptoms: Irregular brown necrotic spots with concentric ring pattern (bullseye target)
Prominent yellow chlorosis surrounding lesions on mature lower foliage
Progressive upward defoliation leaving fruit susceptible to sunscald
Sunken, leathery black cankers on stems and fruit calyx
causes: Overwinters on infected solanaceous crop residues and volunteer weeds
High humidity and temperatures of 75-85°F alternating with dry periods
management: Prune lower foliage (bottom 12-18 inches) to prevent soil contact
Apply organic mulches (straw, plastic) beneath vines to prevent rain splash
Stake or trellis tomatoes to promote rapid canopy drying
Apply protective fungicides (chlorothalonil, copper, or bio-fungicides) preventively

scientific_paper.title: Early blight of potato and tomato: A review of Alternaria solani biology and control
scientific_paper.authors: Kemmitt, G.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Details solanapyrone phytotoxin action inducing chlorotic halos around concentric necrotic foliar rings.

title: Tomato Production and Disease Prevention
publisher: University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources
symptoms: Vigorous pinnately compound green leaves without curling, mottling, or spot necrosis
causes: Optimum calcium/nitrogen balance, consistent moisture, and active pest scouting
management: Stake plants, use drip lines, and mulch soil around root zones

scientific_paper.title: Morphological and functional leaf traits of healthy Solanum lycopersicum
scientific_paper.authors: Heuvelink, E.
scientific_paper.journal: Tomatoes (Crop Production Science in Horticulture, CABI)
scientific_paper.key_finding: Establishes standard leaf area index (LAI), leaf greenness SPAD values, and absence of stress enzymes.

title: Managing Late Blight in Tomato Crops
symptoms: Large, irregularly shaped pale green to dark water-soaked lesions
Delicate white fungal-like mold visible on leaf undersides in humid mornings
Stems show dark brown greasy lesions leading to total vine collapse
Firm, dark, greasy brown rot expanding across green or ripening fruit
causes: Airborne sporangia carried for miles on storm winds from infected fields or volunteer potatoes
Favored by cool, cloudy, persistently wet weather (60-70°F)
management: Inspect fields at least twice weekly during cool wet spells
Immediately rogue out and bag infected plants to prevent sporangia dispersal
Apply protectant fungicides (chlorothalonil, fixed copper, cyazofamid) before rain events

scientific_paper.title: Phytophthora infestans on tomato: Global population shifts and disease forecasting
scientific_paper.authors: Nowicki, M., Foolad, M. R., Nowakowska, M., & Kozik, E. U.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Investigates US-22 and US-23 oomycete lineages driving rapid water-soaked petiole collapse in Solanum.

title: Septoria Leaf Spot of Tomato
symptoms: Numerous small (1.5-3 mm) circular spots with grayish-white centers and dark margins
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) embedded in the center of mature lesions
Lower leaves turn completely yellow, wither, and drop prematurely
Fruit is rarely infected directly, but severe defoliation leads to sunscald
causes: Fungus overwinters in solanaceous plant debris and weed hosts (e.g., horsenettle)
Spreads upward by splashing water during rain or overhead watering
management: Remove lower leaves up to the first fruit cluster as plants mature
Apply deep straw or plastic mulch to create a physical barrier against soil splash
Rotate out of solanaceous crops for a minimum of 2-3 years
Treat early with copper fungicides or chlorothalonil upon appearance of first spots

scientific_paper.title: Biology and epidemiology of Septoria lycopersici Speg. on tomato
scientific_paper.authors: Douglas, D. R., & Pavek, J. J.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Dissects pycnidia fruiting body morphogenesis within circular circular lesions possessing distinctive dark brown margins.

title: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus Management
symptoms: Upward cupping and curling of leaf margins on young apical growth
Marked reduction in leaf size ('little leaf' appearance)
Prominent interveinal chlorosis and yellowing of leaf blades
Severe plant stunting, bushy erect habit, and premature flower drop resulting in total yield loss
causes: Transmitted persistently by the silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
Not seed-borne or mechanically transmitted through touch or pruning tools
management: Plant TYLCV-resistant tomato hybrids (e.g., Tygress, Charger, Tribute)
Manage whitefly vector populations using reflective silver mulches and insecticidal soaps/oils
Use fine insect netting (50-mesh) on nursery transplant houses
Immediately eradicate and bag virus-infected plants to limit whitefly acquisition

scientific_paper.title: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus: Biology, epidemiology, and management
scientific_paper.authors: Moriones, E., & Navas-Castillo, J.
scientific_paper.key_finding: Uncovers Bemisia tabaci whitefly circulative transmission dynamics and severe leaf curling/stunting.
